title: Background Sync
description: Implement background sync strategies for offline mutations and data consistency in React Query.

data.text: When a user submits a form while offline, the mutation fails immediately. React Query does not have built-in offline mutation queuing, but you can implement it by storing failed mutations locally and replaying them when connectivity returns. This pattern â€” called background sync â€” makes your application resilient to any network condition.
The best offline experience is the one the user doesn't notice. They should be able to work, submit, and continue â€” and everything syncs when they're back online.

A mutation queue is a list of pending mutations stored locally. Each entry contains the mutation type, payload, timestamp, and a unique ID. When the app detects it is back online, it processes the queue in order, removing each entry only after a successful server response.

terms.definition: A local list of mutations that failed due to offline status, to be replayed when connectivity returns.
The process of replaying queued mutations in the background after connectivity is restored.
Updating the UI cache immediately before the server confirms the mutation, with rollback on failure.

data.title: Offline mutation queue with localStorage
data.content: A complete offline mutation queue pattern using localStorage and event listeners.

data.text: Users can trigger the same mutation multiple times while offline. Always deduplicate by ID to avoid duplicate entries when the queue is replayed. Also maintain insertion order so mutations are applied to the server in the same sequence the user created them.

data.title: Always Deduplicate
data.text: If the user adds the same todo twice while offline, replaying the queue without deduplication will create duplicates on the server. Use a Set or check for existing IDs before pushing to the queue.

data.title: Deduplicated mutation queue helper
data.content: Deduplicate by ID before adding to the queue to prevent duplicates on replay.

data.text: For progressive web apps, the Service Worker Background Sync API provides a more reliable mechanism. Instead of relying on the `online` event (which can fire multiple times), the service worker queues sync requests and replays them when the browser detects connectivity. This works even if the user closes the tab and reopens it later.

data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant App
    participant MutationQueue
    participant ServiceWorker
    participant Server
    User->>App: Submit form (offline)
    App->>MutationQueue: Store mutation
    App->>User: Show 'queued' indicator
    Note over ServiceWorker: Browser detects network
    ServiceWorker->>MutationQueue: Read pending mutations
    loop For each queued mutation
        MutationQueue->>Server: Replay mutation
        Server-->>MutationQueue: Success response
        MutationQueue->>MutationQueue: Remove from queue
    end
    MutationQueue->>App: Update cache via message
    App->>User: Show 'synced' confirmation
data.caption: Background sync flow: mutations are queued locally, then replayed by the service worker when the network returns.

data.title: Start Simple
data.text: Begin with the localStorage queue pattern. Add service worker background sync once your app needs to handle tab closes or extended offline periods. The service worker approach is more robust but requires more setup.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Background Sync System
data.description: Implement a background sync system for a todo app. Queue mutations when offline, show a pending count, and replay when the user comes back online.
steps: Create a queue array in localStorage to store pending mutations.
Create an addMutation function that checks navigator.onLine before executing.
When offline, store the mutation in the queue and optimistically update the cache.
Listen for the 'online' event and call processQueue to replay all pending mutations.
Show a badge with the number of pending mutations in the UI.
Clear the queue only after all mutations have been confirmed by the server.
data.expectedOutcome: Users can add todos while offline, see a pending count, and watch them sync automatically when the connection returns.

items.question: Do I need a service worker for background sync?
items.answer: No. The localStorage + online event pattern works well for most apps. Service worker background sync is better for PWAs where the tab might be closed and reopened while offline.

items.question: What if a queued mutation fails on replay?
items.answer: Handle the error gracefully: remove successfully replayed mutations from the queue, leave failed ones, and notify the user. Consider adding a manual retry button for failed items.

items.question: Can I use background sync with optimistic updates?
items.answer: Yes. Apply the optimistic update immediately when the user triggers the mutation. If the queued replay later fails, roll back the optimistic update and show an error.

data.title: Background Sync Key Points
points: Queue mutations when offline using localStorage or IndexedDB.
Replay the queue in order when connectivity returns.
Deduplicate queued mutations by ID to prevent duplicates.
Combine with optimistic updates for perceived performance.
Service worker background sync is more robust for PWAs.
data.takeaway: Background sync makes React Query applications resilient to network interruptions.
